title: ticfac Phase 3: finish the extraction and run it in anger
description:
SPEC §12 Phase 3. Rough scope — plan the child ticks at the START of this epic,
not now.

Phase 2 built the herdr executor and proved it on a throwaway repository. Phase 3
is what makes it the real thing: the removal that turns "copied" into
"extracted", and a production run that turns "it works on a demo" into "it runs
our work".

Carried in from av8's residuals, which are the honest list of what is NOT done:

- **The retirements** (av8 ticks 4l2, 1ya). Delete the execution packages and
  the factory from ticks. Blocked on the dispatch gap below. Until they land,
  `tk factory` is a full second implementation and the sandbox loop is still
  `tk`.
- **Cross-repo dispatch** (av8 tick hk7). `tk herd spawn` always creates a
  worktree of the repo whose tracker holds the tick, so a tick whose work is in
  another checkout cannot be dispatched — its branch is uncollectable and
  ungated. Decide the shape: a declared target repo, or refuse at PLANNING time.
  This is the keystone: the retirements and the upstream bundle merges both need
  it.
- **A PRODUCTION epic on the herdr executor.** av8's proof is a demo repo whose
  implement ticks write one note each. Run a real epic — ideally this one.
- **The unfinished robustness edges.** Capabilities are not refreshed on
  reconnect; the read-only socket probe builds a client with no protocol
  warning; `record.Protocol` is written but never read back for a decision;
  layer 3 of the completion design (consuming herdr's push stream as a wait)
  was deliberately not wired.
- **The two-readers discipline has a third path.** `internal/cli/cloud.go`
  reaches ticks data ungated, bypassing the `internal/tk` client that decision
  rests on.
- **The pinned contract still does not cover `[testing.commands]` or
  `[roles.*]`** — av8 tick 8ug's core ask, filed upstream, unresolved.

Read `.tick/logs/herd/av8/RETRO.md` before planning: it carries the full
residual list with file-level detail, and the two patterns worth keeping — a
guarantee that a test can falsify survives review, and one resting on prose does
not.
notes:
2026-09-15 10:47 - A3 and A4 amended the same day they were written, to match what is actually right rather than what was first guessed.

A3 dropped the feed HEARTBEAT. A heartbeat written by a timer goroutine keeps ticking when the reconciler's main loop is wedged, so it does not detect the one thing a heartbeat would be for; a pid plus its OS start time already answers liveness exactly; and progress is answered by the age of the last feed event, which ticfac status reports. A periodic line would also have added noise to every feed subscriber for no new information.

A4 now says what is possible. SIGKILL cannot be caught, so no process can write a terminal line for its own SIGKILL. That death is still mechanically visible — the pidfile it could not remove names a process that is gone, and status reads dead.
acceptance_criteria:
[A1] A run survives an operator observing it: git fetch in the run's checkout, ticfac findings, and reading the branch do not end or corrupt the run, proven by a test that does all three mid-run.
[A2] A run-state conflict does not end a run: the reconciler continues against the refreshed state and fails only after a bounded number of consecutive conflicts on one write.
[A3] 'Is this run alive?' is answered by ticfac itself — a pidfile recording the process start time, and `ticfac status` — so a killed run reads dead immediately and a reused pid never reads alive.
[A4] Every death the process can observe (an operational error, a panic, SIGINT or SIGTERM) leaves its cause in the run's own log and a run_died line in the feed; a SIGKILL death, which can write nothing, reads dead from `ticfac status`.
[A5] Every attempt's prose report is archived in the run's records, whatever its verdict, and survives worktree teardown.
[A6] A closeout attempt commits its own learnings and the run integrates them; no role is told a boundary stricter than the one it is judged against.
[A7] With several surviving attempts of one tick, the run adopts the latest adoptable one.
[A8] Every other child of this epic is closed or carries a recorded reason it was deferred.
